strongest_angle: Engineering research from September 2026 reveals that flexible steel shafts in heavy-duty engines redistribute hydrodynamic support across multiple journal bearings, altering oil film stability.

key_facts.fact: A study published on September 18, 2026, by Yulin Zhang and colleagues analyzes a three-disk, four-support bearing-rotor system to understand how shaft flexibility affects hydrodynamic support.
Flexible steel shafts in heavy-duty engines rest on multiple oil-lubricated journal bearings, which generate pressurized films to prevent direct metal-to-metal contact during rotation.
In a four-support bearing-rotor system, the bending of the shaft simultaneously changes the journal attitudes at each of the four support locations, redistributing the oil film pressure.
